front.title: Control Plane of Source Address Validation Architecture-eXternal (SAVA-X)

abstract.t: Because the Internet forwards packets according to the IP destination address, packet forwarding generally occurs without examining the source address. Consequently, malicious attacks have been launched using spoofed source addresses. The inter-domain source address validation architecture represents an effort to enhance the Internet by employing state machines to generate consistent tags. When two end hosts in different address domains (ADs) of an IPv6 network communicate with each other, tags are appended to the packets to identify the authenticity of the IPv6 source address.
